f.title: Ensure reference and biosimilar products remain safe and effective throughout their life cycle
f.statement: Manufacturers of both reference products (PR) and biosimilars are responsible for ensuring that their products remain safe and effective throughout their life cycle, avoiding significant changes in individual products.
f.applicability: Biosimilar medicinal products registered in Argentina under Disposición ANMAT 7729/11 (well-characterised recombinant proteins and peptides). Original language Spanish.

f.title: Closely monitor biosimilar safety and efficacy in all approved indications with continuous post-marketing benefit-risk evaluation
f.statement: As with all medicines, close monitoring of the safety and efficacy of a biosimilar in all approved indications is necessary, together with continuous evaluation of the benefit-risk relationship, in the post-marketing phase.
f.applicability: Biosimilar medicinal products registered in Argentina under Disposición ANMAT 7729/11 (well-characterised recombinant proteins and peptides). Original language Spanish.

f.title: Incorporate safety monitoring or risk minimisation measures imposed on the reference product or class into the biosimilar PV plan
f.statement: Any specific safety monitoring or risk minimisation measure imposed on the reference product or the product class must be incorporated into the pharmacovigilance plan of the relevant biosimilar, unless it can be convincingly justified that this is not necessary.
f.applicability: Biosimilar medicinal products registered in Argentina under Disposición ANMAT 7729/11 (well-characterised recombinant proteins and peptides). Original language Spanish.
f.exceptions: Unless it can be convincingly justified that incorporation is not necessary.

f.statement: Safety information must be evaluated scientifically, and this must include evaluation of the frequency and cause of adverse events.

f.title: Submit a PV plan (safety specification, PV activities, risk minimisation) with the MA application or when a post-marketing safety concern arises
f.statement: The manufacturer must submit a pharmacovigilance plan describing the safety specification, pharmacovigilance activities and risk minimisation activities at the time the marketing authorisation application is submitted or whenever a safety problem arises after marketing.
f.applicability: Biosimilar medicinal products registered in Argentina under Disposición ANMAT 7729/11 (well-characterised recombinant proteins and peptides). Original language Spanish.

f.statement: The safety specification must describe the important identified or potential safety problems for the reference product and for the substance class, as well as those specific to the biosimilar.

f.title: Include residual uncertainties (e.g. new excipient or device) in the PV plan and follow them up post-marketing
f.statement: Where doubts about the biosimilar persist, for example due to the use of a new excipient or device, they must be included in the pharmacovigilance plan and followed up after marketing.

f.title: Have an adequate PV system with a qualified person and means for ADR reporting from all countries of marketing in place at authorisation
f.statement: Manufacturers must ensure that, at the time of marketing authorisation, they have an adequate pharmacovigilance system, including the services of a qualified person responsible for monitoring pharmacovigilance activities and the means necessary to report adverse reactions occurring in any of the countries in which the product is marketed.

f.title: Maintain a system ensuring specific identification (traceability) of the biosimilar
f.statement: As with all biological products, an adequate system ensuring the specific identification of the biosimilar (traceability) in accordance with current regulations is essential.

f.title: Include brand name, manufacturer and batch number, besides the INN, in ADR reports for biological products
f.statement: In addition to the international non-proprietary name (INN), adverse reaction reports for any biological product must also include all other important identifiers, such as the brand name, the manufacturer name and the batch number, in addition to compliance with the requirements of current pharmacovigilance regulations.
